COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
16.04.2026 CLCON No. 102 of 2026
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J. 
This Contempt Petition has been filed 
alleging wilful disobedience of the Order 
dated 23.12.2025, passed in Writ Petition 
No. 3421 (S/S) of 2018, “Smt. Reena Rani 
Vs. State of Uttarakhand and Others”. 
2. By the Order dated 23.12.2025, the 
following direction was issued :-
“10. Accordingly, the writ petition is 
allowed. The impugned order dated 
01.10.2018 passed by respondent 
no.4 is quashed. The respondents are 
directed to reinstate the petitioner 
forthwith and to give all the 
consequential benefits which she is 
entitled as per law.”
3. Heard Mr. Tapan Singh, learned 
counsel for the petitioner. 
4. Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate, submitted 
that the petitioner supplied the e-certified 
copy of the order dated 23.12.2025 to the 
respondent no.3 along with an application 
on 12.01.2026, but, the respondent no.3 
has deliberately not complied with the Order 
dated 23.12.2025 till date. 
5. It is prima facie case of wilful  disobedience of the Order dated 
23.12.2025. 
6. Notice is being issued to Tarun Pant, 
District Education Officer, Pithoragarh, the 
respondent no.3. He is directed to appear 
before this Court through video 
conferencing on 11.05.2026 at 10:30 a.m. 
and show cause as to why proceedings for
contempt of court should not be initiated 
against him. 
7. Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate, has 
sought one week’s time for steps. 
8. List on 11.05.2026 at 10:30 a.m. 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.)
16.04.2026
Shiv/

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLCON No. 102 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, learned Standing 
Counsel for the respondent/contemnor.
3. Mr. Tarun Pant, District Education 
Officer, Pithoragarh is present in Court.
4. Apparently, the order of the Writ Court 
is not complied with whereby the writ petition 
was allowed and the impugned order was 
quashed and the respondent was directed to 
reinstate the petitioner forthwith with all 
consequential benefits which the petitioner is 
entitled as per law. The writ Court passed the 
order on 23.12.2025 and almost four months 
have been passed and during this period 
neither the judgment has been complied with 
nor assailed by way of filing special appeal 
though the limitation has also been expired.
5. In such view of the matter this Court 
has no option except to frame charge against 
the respondent, who is present in Court. This 
Court is framing the following charge against 
the respondent/contemnor:-
“The respondent/contemnor Mr. Tarun 
Pant, District Education Officer of Pithoragarh 
committed contempt of this Court by willfully 
disobeying the order of the Writ Court dated 
23.12.2025 passed in WPMS No. 3421 of 2018, 
despite having knowledge of the same.”
6. Since, charge has been framed in the 
presence of contemnor, let he may file 
response within a week for the aforesaid 
charge and to show cause why he may be  punished for contempt of Court.
7. Put up this matter on 04.06.2026. On that 
day the respondent/contemnor shall remain 
present in Court.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
22.05.2026
Parul

Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel along with

whereby Co-ordinate Bench of this Court framed charges 
against the respondent-contemnor, Mr. Tarun Pant, for 
willfully disobeying the order of the Writ Court dated 
23.12.2025 passed in WPSS No.3421 of 2018, despite 
having full knowledge of the same.
4. Respondent no.3 has filed a response affidavit dated 
29.05.2026, annexing therewith the order dated 
27.05.2026, whereby petitioner has now been reinstated 
in service pursuant to the order passed by the Writ 
Court.

as Assistant Teacher, Government Primary School, Cham 
Dungara, Block Gangolihat, District Pithoragarh.

compliance has not been fully made, as the Writ Court 
directed the respondent to grant all consequential 
benefits to which she is entitled as per law.
7. Mr. Tarun Pant, respondent no.3-contemnor,  2
submitted that after receipt of the salary for the month of 
June, Deputy Education Officer, being the drawing and 
disbursing authority of the petitioner, may release all 
consequential benefits as per law to the petitioner.
8. List on 08.07.2026, enabling learned counsel for the 
respondent-contemnor to fully comply with the order.
9. The personal appearance of respondent no.3, Mr. 
Tarun Pant, District Education Officer, Pithoragarh, is 
hereby exempted until further orders.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)

similar.quote: “Civil Contempt No. 117/2006 Hon'ble J.C.S. Rawat, J. This Contempt Petition has been filed under the Contempt of Court's Act to punish the contemnors for not complying the order dated 09.12.2005 passed by this court in Writ Petition No. 277/2005 (S/B in which the court has directed the respondent to consider and dispose of Annexure 1 representation dated 15.01.2004 of the petitioner, if it was received and is pending…”

notes.disclaimer: Is case ke orders mein vishay saaf nahi likha (zyaadatar tareekh / kaam-kaaj). Ye faisle orders ke khaas shabdon se mile hain, isliye milaan kamzor ho sakta hai — advocate jaanch lein. Quote faisle ka asli paragraph hai. Behtar nateeje ke liye Khoj mein case ki baat likhein.
